matches.rationale: GT 1 concerns inflated benchmark results in Figure 9 and Section 4.2 showing unrealistically high compression performance. None of the findings identify issues with Figure 9's accuracy numbers or question the plausibility of the reported benchmark results.

GT 2 identifies the contradiction in Section 3.4 between claiming 2× latency reduction while reporting doubled prefill computation overhead. Finding 1 directly captures this same inconsistency, documenting the mutually exclusive claims about O(m n_c) linear vs O(n_c^2 + n_c m/2) quadratic complexity and the ~2× prefill cost.

GT 3 concerns the experimental design choice in Section 4.1 to apply non-uniform head-budget allocation to baselines, potentially biasing comparisons. None of the findings address this methodological protocol issue or question the fairness of baseline configurations.

GT 4 identifies exaggerated claims in the Abstract ('negligible performance loss', 'significantly outperforms') that are not fully substantiated. Finding 4 documents specific numerical inconsistencies between the Abstract's claims (2–3× cache reduction, 1.5× latency, 100K tokens) and the body's stronger claims (3–4×, 2×, 170K), revealing the same issue of overstated abstract claims.
GT 5 concerns a fabricated reference to Corallo et al. [14] in Section 5 (Related Work). None of the findings identify issues with citations or reference fabrication in the related work section.

GT 6 identifies the omission of ethical discussion in the main body regarding privacy leakage risks shown in Section 4.3/Table 1. While findings mention Table 1 data issues, none specifically address the missing ethical implications discussion or mitigation strategies in the main text.

GT 7 concerns overly positive rhetoric in the Conclusion ('effectively optimizes', 'consistently outperforms', 'negligible performance loss') without sufficient caveats. None of the findings specifically analyze the Conclusion's rhetorical presentation or identify unqualified claims there.

GT 8 identifies misalignment between Introduction claims (70% eviction with maintained accuracy) and mixed Section 4.2 results. While Finding 4 addresses Abstract-Introduction inconsistencies, it focuses on numerical metrics rather than the Introduction's accuracy claims versus experimental outcomes mismatch.

GT 9 concerns optimistic/under-reported computational overhead numbers in Figure 8b (compression time and peak memory). None of the findings question the plausibility of Figure 8b's overhead measurements or suggest they are unrealistically low.

GT 10 identifies overly positive rhetorical language in the Introduction ('novel', 'particularly benefits', 'robust generalization', 'seamlessly integrates'). None of the findings analyze the Introduction's rhetorical presentation or identify inflated language without supporting caveats.

GT 11 concerns missing IRB/consent disclosures and conflict-of-interest statements in the main body for sensitive datasets. None of the findings identify missing ethical disclosures, IRB statements, or funding transparency issues in the main text.

GT 12 concerns removal/alteration of Table 1 entries showing privacy leakage (phone number revelation). While Finding 3 mentions issues with result tables, it addresses impossible identical-cache divergence in Figures 22-23, not Table 1's privacy example data integrity.

GT 13 identifies inconsistencies in Section 3.2's attention matrix dimensions and Equation (2)'s max operation ranges. Finding 2 directly captures these same errors: the mismatch between declared dimensions and equation indices, and the swapped Q/K tensor shapes relative to Algorithm 1.

GT 14 concerns systematic exaggeration of KVzip's performance advantage over baselines in Section 4 figures. Finding 3 identifies impossible divergence at ratio 1.0 in Figures 22-23 where all methods should be identical, revealing systematic data integrity issues in the comparative results presentation.

GT 15 concerns omission or weakening of Appendix Section B's ethical implications, broader impacts, privacy risks, and limitations discussion. None of the findings identify missing or inadequate content in the Appendix's ethical/limitations sections.
